programme.title: Heatwave
programme.desc: An alarming vision of Britain caught in the grip of an environmental and social nightmare. It is summer 2006, and temperatures have topped 100 degrees, with no end in sight.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Three members of the Brighton and Hove (Actually) Gay Men's Chorus square up to a trio of postgraduates of Brasenose College, Oxford. They compete to draw together the connections between things which, at first glance, seem utterly random.

programme.title: Stonehenge: The Lost Circle Revealed
programme.desc: Professor Alice Roberts follows a decade-long historical quest to reveal a hidden secret of the famous bluestones of Stonehenge. Using cutting-edge research, a dedicated team of archaeologists led by Prof Mike Parker Pearson have painstaking compiled evidence to fill in a 400-year gap in knowledge of the bluestones, and to show that the original stones of Britain's most iconic monument had a previous life.

programme.title: Universe
programme.sub-title: Alien Worlds: The Search for Second Earth
programme.desc: Humans have long gazed up at the night sky, wondering whether other lifeforms and intelligences could be thriving on worlds far beyond our own. Answering that question seemed fated to remain pure speculation.

programme.title: The Nazis: A Warning From History
programme.desc: We reveal the extraordinary popularity of both Hitler and the Nazis, as well as the astonishing degree of voluntary support ordinary Germans gave the infamous Gestapo.

programme.title: One Foot in Arthur's Seat
programme.desc: Actor Ian Richardson walks up the hill to Arthur's Seat, which overlooks the city of Edinburgh, as he did during lunch hours as a bored office clerk 50 years ago.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.sub-title: W Stephen Gilbert Remembers... Only Connect
programme.desc: W Stephen Gilbert looks back on the 1979 BBC drama 'Only Connect', portraying a homosexual relationship - including the challenges of making it and its impact since the original broadcast.

programme.title: The Other Side
programme.desc: Young academic Graham visits the elderly John Bury to learn more about pioneering socialist and gay rights campaigner Edward Carpenter for his thesis on the early UK Labour movement. Graham wants the facts but discovers, to his advantage, that people are not text books.

programme.title: Alison Steadman Remembers... Girl
programme.desc: National treasure Alison Steadman tells the story of one of the most groundbreaking and yet also most overlooked moments in British television. Despite the popular perception that Channel 4's Brookside broadcast TV's first lesbian kiss in 1994, in reality it was Alison and Myra Frances who first broke the taboo, 20 years earlier in the 1974 drama Girl.

programme.title: Second City Firsts
programme.desc: Just as she is about to leave the army, Jackie has an encounter with an old lover. Stars Alison Steadman in an early TV role.

programme.title: Vienna: Empire, Dynasty and Dream
programme.desc: Simon Sebag Montefiore tells the story of Vienna triumphant, after the Ottoman threat receded at the end of the 17th century. The city was rebuilt. No longer an outpost defending the West from Islamic invaders, the Habsburgs vowed their empire and imperial capital would become the most glittering in the world. The Habsburg emperors transformed the city from a fortress into a great cultural capital.

programme.title: Horizon
programme.sub-title: Tim Peake Special: How to Be an Astronaut
programme.desc: In December 2015, Tim Peake became Britain's first astronaut on board the International Space Station. For two years, he had been filming a video diary for Horizon as he prepared to leave. From family life to the rigorous training, this is an intimate portrait and remarkable insight into the world of an astronaut.

programme.title: The Magnificent Seven
programme.desc: A Mexican village is at the mercy of Calvera, the leader of a band of outlaws. The townspeople, too afraid to fight for themselves, hire seven American gunslingers to free them from the bandits' raids. The professional gunmen train the villagers to defend themselves, then plan a trap for the evil Calvera.

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Robert Hughes considers how the Civil War industrialised society, bringing steam power, the Brooklyn Bridge, plutocrats and an urban underclass. Nostalgia for loss entered the culture and brought the Museum Age.

programme.title: Chuck Berry in Concert
programme.desc: Legendary rock and roller Chuck Berry performs at the BBC Television Theatre in 1972. 'Johnny B Goode', 'Roll Over Beethoven' and 'Nadine' are just some of the highlights of this concert, shown in an extended cut. This version includes, for the first time, an epic rendition of 'My Ding-a-Ling' that carries all before it and raises innuendo to an art form.
